packages/openviking-pi/package.json lists @modelcontextprotocol/client at an exact version and node_modules is not in the tree, so npm ci --ignore-scripts must run in packages/openviking-pi before the first start.

The extension needs an OpenViking server with viking://~ home alias support. The endpoint and the key resolve from OPENVIKING_* variables, ~/.openviking/ovcli.conf or ~/.openviking/ov.conf; the kit writes none of them and has no field for them. Context takeover, off by default, trims history only when the server confirms Working Memory for the commit; OpenViking v0.5.0 and later do. OpenViking v0.5.2 and later answer a root key on /mcp with HTTP 403, so the openviking_* tools need a user or admin key.
Pi 1.3.0 isolated qualification checks the file-source resolver, factory loading and all package tests with candidate dependencies. Capture, recall and tools against a live server remain unverified.

The extension captures no tool result output unless captureToolResults is true. With it on, each tool part is capped by captureToolMaxChars and the server externalizes larger output. Not measured: the growth of session storage and the effect on memory extraction.
Run npm ci --ignore-scripts in packages/agentcore-memory-core before loading the extension. The extension imports that shared core, and the lock file of the core installs the AWS SDK.

The owner supplies the AgentCore Memory resource, the IAM user of the person with its namespace-scoped inline policy, the access key and the person config file. The kit creates none of them; the owner tool packages/agentcore-memory-admin renders the policy and the person config.
Offline fake-core tests cover the recall hook, the propose tool and its confirmation. Not verified: a Pi session with live AWS recall or propose.

The package.json of version 0.7.27 limits os to linux and cpu to x64 and arm64, and its postinstall script stops on another platform. The kit has no computer-use module for macOS; that choice is open.

The registry tarball of version 0.7.24 was read. The read covered package.json, npm/install.js, the README and the Pi setup reference of the skill. A file comparison with the tarball of version 0.7.27 found changes only in package.json, the README files, the skill and the extension, which adds the read-only tool get_tree_page; npm/install.js is unchanged. The extension source and the release binaries were not reviewed.

The postinstall script npm/install.js downloads the release binaries of the same version from the GitHub releases of agent-sh/computer-use-linux. It checks each binary against its published sha256 file. The install therefore needs network access. Without the downloaded binary, the extension looks for COMPUTER_USE_LINUX_BIN, then for computer-use-linux on PATH.

The tools need a graphical Linux session with the AT-SPI accessibility bridge and an input backend that the doctor tool of the package reports ready. The kit installs none of them; the kit doctor reports the readiness that the doctor of the package gives. The setup tools of the package change the desktop settings of the user.

The tools observe and act on the live desktop of the user. Screenshots and accessibility trees that a tool returns go into the conversation and so to the model provider. A loaded extension does not prove that a tool works on a given desktop.

The module needs an OpenKnowledge server of the user with HTTP Basic authentication in front of /mcp and the document API. The kit installs no server and writes no credential; the user exports OPENKNOWLEDGE_USERNAME and OPENKNOWLEDGE_PASSWORD.
No macOS run of install.sh --with okknow, of okknow setup or of the CLI against a server. The Linux checks of the kit run the CLI and the installer offline with a scratch home and no server.

The mcp-adapter.json entry uses the header command form !<path> auth-header, read in the source of pi-mcp-adapter 7.0.0 (the kit pin): a leading ! runs the command in a shell with a 10-second limit and uses its trimmed output. No session with that adapter connected to the server through that entry.
